findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-18.result.json, roadmaps[EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves].layers[EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.1:biduality] and layers[EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.1], target 'Finite-level ordinary duals over the self-injective rings ℤ/ℓⁿ and derived duals with Ext terms over ℤ_ℓ'
findings.claim: The target is marked 'absent', and the note says only semisimple-ring injectivity (ℤ/ℓ) and a Frobenius-algebra criterion exist, 'self-injectivity of ℤ/ℓⁿ for n ≥ 2 is not stated'. The note misses that Mathlib proves the finite-level ordinary duality for finite abelian groups of exponent n. The duality takes values in a monoid with enough n-th roots of unity: biduality holds, the dual is exact because characters of a subgroup extend, and the dual is (noncanonically) isomorphic to the group itself. For finite ℤ/ℓⁿ-modules this is exactly the ordinary ℤ/ℓⁿ-duality, after identifying μ_{ℓⁿ} with ℤ/ℓⁿ by a primitive root. Self-injectivity of ℤ/ℓⁿ also follows in a few lines: apply the character-extension theorem to the ideals of ℤ/ℓⁿ, then Baer's criterion. The ordinary-dual half of the target is therefore partly in Mathlib, and 'absent' overstates the gap. The label is also inconsistent with the audit's own practice: EDC.8's third target is 'partial' on related/special-case declarations alone, while this target already cites a special-case declaration (Module.injective_of_isSemisimpleRing).
findings.evidence: Mathlib/GroupTheory/FiniteAbelian/Duality.lean at 082e2d3, with variables (G M : Type*) [CommGroup G] [Finite G] [CommMonoid M] [hM : HasEnoughRootsOfUnity M (Monoid.exponent G)]. Line 151: 'noncomputable def monoidHomMonoidHomEquiv : ((G →* Mˣ) →* Mˣ) ≃* G', 'The MulEquiv between the double dual ... and itself'. Line 81: 'theorem monoidHom_mulEquiv_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity : Nonempty ((G →* Mˣ) ≃* G)'. Also Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/FiniteAbelian/PontryaginDuality.lean:174 'def doubleDualEquiv : α ≃+ AddChar (AddChar α ℂ) ℂ' for finite α. Baer's criterion is Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Injective.lean:401 'protected theorem injective (h : Module.Baer R Q) : Module.Injective R Q'. HasEnoughRootsOfUnity holds for separably closed fields with n invertible (Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/AlgebraicallyClosed.lean:29), e.g. ℂ.
findings.fix: In both layers (EDC.1:biduality and the parent EDC.1), change this target's library from 'absent' to 'partial'. Add as declarations MonoidHom.domRestrict_surjective (Mathlib/GroupTheory/FiniteAbelian/Duality.lean:107, fit 'related') and CommGroup.monoidHomMonoidHomEquiv (Mathlib/GroupTheory/FiniteAbelian/Duality.lean:151, fit 'related'), keeping Module.injective_of_isSemisimpleRing. Replace the last clause of the note with: 'Mathlib proves duality for finite abelian groups with values in a monoid with enough roots of unity: biduality and exactness of the dual, the latter as extension of characters from subgroups. For finite ℤ/ℓⁿ-modules this is the finite-level ordinary duality in character form, and self-injectivity of ℤ/ℓⁿ follows from it by Baer's criterion. Missing: the ℤ/ℓⁿ-linear statement, duality for complexes of sheaves, and the derived dual with Ext terms over ℤ_ℓ.' The layer verdicts stay 'not built'.

findings.claim: The note says 'Only the Rees algebra exists; no blowups of schemes.' Tau Ceti has a proved lattice-level blowup formula. Blowing up a point of a plumbed 4-manifold, with the total-transform identification, makes the new intersection form the orthogonal sum of the old form and ⟨−1⟩, and the exceptional class has square −1 and is orthogonal to the pulled-back lattice. This is the linear-algebra shadow of the point-blowup formula on a surface, which is EDC.4's own acceptance test ('blowing up a point on a surface'). It is not a blowup of schemes and does not change the 'absent' label, but it is nearer material than the Rees algebra, and the 'Only' in the note is inaccurate.
